newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa no to surcharge for rates hike.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa no to surcharge for rates hike.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo AG said it has no plans to follow KLM Royal Dutch Airlines and drop its cargo fuel surcharge.
KLM said on December 17 it would raise air cargo rates by five to ten percent in the first quarter of 1997 and drop its present fuel surcharge at the same time.
Lufthansa Cargo spokesman Dietrich Seidl told Reuters: "We will remain with our cargo fuel surcharge.
"We will go ahead with a rates increase of seven to ten percent in March next year but that is independent of a fuel surcharge," he added.
The surcharge would first be dropped when jet fuel prices returned to their levels of summer 1996, he stressed.
Lufthansa Cargo chairman Wilhelm Althen said on November 29 the airline would raise rates in March and August next year to try to improve profitability and stop a fall in air cargo market rates.
Separately, a Lufthansa passenger spokesman said the German airline raised passenger fares by three percent from December 15.
This was in line with an industry agreement reached at a meeting of IATA airlines in mid-November in reaction to higher fuel costs, he added.
